extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (K-12 schools, postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, compliance officers, institutional legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements that recipients of Department of Education funds must follow to operate education programs free from sex discrimination, including recordkeeping, training-materials transparency, notification duties, and grievance/response obligations under §§106.8 and 106.44-.46.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of notifications to Title IX Coordinator (§106.8(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each notification the Title IX Coordinator receives of information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination (including notifications under §106.44(c)(1) or (2)), a recipient must maintain records documenting the actions it took to meet its obligations in §106.44, including its prompt and effective response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.8(f)(2) to replace language referencing an “incident” with the cited “notification” phrasing to align with §106.44(c). Records must document the recipient's prompt and effective response and the specific actions taken under §106.44(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period — seven years
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department maintains that seven years is an appropriate length of time that records must be maintained under the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may retain records longer if they choose or due to other legal obligations; retention is not tied to student enrollment length or litigation potential because a uniform threshold is easier to administer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain records of dismissed complaints and informal resolutions (§106.8(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to maintain information regarding the dismissal of a complaint or an informal resolution process that ends without a finding or admission of responsibility under §106.8(f)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department declined to require deletion or correction of such records because maintaining these records is necessary to demonstrate compliance with Title IX. If a judicial determination changes the recipient's determination, that change must be included in the maintained records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training materials public inspection requirement (§106.8(f)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must make all materials used to provide training under §106.8(d) available upon request for inspection by members of the public, regardless of whether the recipient maintains a website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule removed a requirement to post training materials on a website but kept a public inspection requirement. This includes slides and records from continuing professional development; a certificate of completion alone is insufficient. Recipients can formalize how inspection requests are made and the method of inspection (e.g., on-site with a representative present).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on using third‑party proprietary training materials
rubrics_metrics.description: If a third‑party provider containing proprietary information refuses to permit public inspection of training materials, the recipient cannot use those materials to meet its training obligations under §106.8(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing abrogates third‑party intellectual property rights; recipients must ensure that any third‑party materials they rely on can be made available for public inspection (or choose alternative materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for video testimonials and privacy concerns in training materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Training materials that include video testimonials about individuals' personal experiences are subject to the public inspection requirement, but recipients may control the manner of inspection to protect privacy interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making materials available via public inspection rather than posting online allows recipients to limit distribution (e.g., review on premises), thereby addressing privacy and proprietary concerns; recipients may provide additional context when sharing materials to avoid misunderstanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of proposed pregnancy-specific recordkeeping (§106.8(f)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department removed proposed §106.8(f)(4), which would have required recordkeeping about pregnancy or related conditions, concluding it is unnecessary and risks chilling students/employees from seeking support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR determined compliance regarding pregnancy accommodations can be evaluated through other recordkeeping requirements (§106.8(f)(1)-(2)) and that privacy/confidentiality concerns (FERPA/HIPAA) outweigh the benefits of the proposed provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients' general duty to operate free from sex discrimination (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must ensure it operates its education program or activity free from sex discrimination and must set forth obligations to respond to sex discrimination to fulfill Title IX's mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(a) provides the basis for enforcement; the Department explained that clear regulatory requirements are needed so recipients know and can be held accountable for their obligations to respond and remedy effects of sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of 'actual knowledge' and 'deliberate indifference' standards from enforcement framing
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations modify/remove the prior reliance on 'actual knowledge' and 'deliberate indifference' language and instead focus on duties to respond to information that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters objected or supported the change; the Department explained that the deliberate indifference standard was not included in the proposed regulations and removed to clarify the recipient's response obligations in administrative enforcement contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring for barriers to reporting (§106.44(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must monitor for barriers to reporting sex discrimination in their education program or activity and take steps reasonably calculated to address them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department views monitoring and addressing barriers as necessary to effectuate Title IX because barriers impede complainants from coming forward and limit the recipient's ability to address discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee notification obligations (§106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.44(c), employees are either required to notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, or to provide the contact information of the Title IX Coordinator and information about how to make a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures that information reaches the Title IX Coordinator even if the complainant does not know how to contact them; aligns with the recordkeeping requirement tied to notifications received by the Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of confidential employees and communication of their status (§106.44(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(d) requires recipients to communicate which employees have confidential status and how individuals may make a complaint to the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves avenues for confidential disclosures that will not automatically trigger Coordinator action while ensuring community members know who is confidential and how to report to the Coordinator if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of disclosures at public awareness events (§106.44(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(e) addresses disclosures that occur during public awareness events and governs how a recipient responds to such information about sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public awareness event disclosures are treated distinctively to reconcile their role in prevention/education with recipients' responsibilities to respond appropriately to disclosed information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator action obligations (§106.44(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(f) sets forth requirements for Title IX Coordinators to take specific actions in response to information about sexual harassment or sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department notes §106.44(f) is consistent with existing §106.44(a) duties and is necessary to ensure appropriate institutional responses; see also §106.44(g) and other related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to offer supportive measures (§106.44(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures to complainants and others as part of their response obligations under §106.44(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures are part of the recipient's duties to respond promptly and effectively and to remedy effects of sex discrimination in the education program or activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondisclosure protections and limits (§106.44(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(j) prohibits a recipient from disclosing personally identifiable information obtained in the course of complying with the Title IX regulations except in limited circumstances and permits compliance with other Federal laws or regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explains that nondisclosure protections are necessary to prevent chilling effects on reporting; §106.44(j) also allows disclosures required by other federal or state laws to the extent not in conflict with Title IX, and cross-references FERPA and other privacy obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against parties' unauthorized disclosure of evidence (§106.45(f)(4)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(f)(4)(iii) requires a recipient to take reasonable steps to prevent and address the parties' unauthorized disclosure of information and evidence obtained solely through the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This duty complements §106.44(j)'s nondisclosure protections and helps preserve confidentiality and integrity of grievance evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of complaints finding responsibility for sexual assault
rubrics_metrics.description: The recordkeeping requirement includes records documenting grievances under §106.45 (and if applicable §106.46), including complaints in which the respondent is found responsible for sexual assault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such recordkeeping documents the outcome of grievance procedures; the Department notes it lacks authority to require a respondent found responsible to register as a sex offender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative enforcement procedural safeguards (termination of federal funds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before terminating, refusing, or discontinuing Federal financial assistance, the Department must make an express finding of noncompliance on the record, notify the recipient, attempt voluntary resolution, and provide opportunity for hearing and judicial review (20 U.S.C. 1682-1683; 34 CFR 100.7(d), 100.8(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR provides notice and opportunities to voluntarily resolve noncompliance during investigations or compliance reviews; resolution agreements are negotiated and tailored to the recipient and findings.
